stats.label: Time spent on scheduling and admin

blocks.text: Why Gmail is the primary tool for recruiters on Mac

Most recruiters on Mac rely on Gmail because it integrates with almost every ATS and calendar tool. Since there is no official native Gmail app, you are likely using it in Chrome or Safari. You can turn your Gmail tab into a standalone app by going to File > Add to Dock in Safari. This keeps your inbox separate from your other browser tabs. It helps you focus on candidate responses without the distraction of open research tabs.
Essential Gmail keyboard shortcuts for recruiters

Keyboard shortcuts are the easiest way to save time. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts to turn them on. Once enabled, press Shift + / to see the full list. As a recruiter, you should master a few specific keys to move through your inbox faster. Use c to compose a new email, r to reply, and a to reply all to candidates. Use j and k to move down or up through your emails. These small actions save minutes every hour when you process hundreds of emails a day.

items: c: Compose a new message to a candidate
e: Archive the current thread to clear your inbox
r: Reply to the hiring manager or recruiter
a: Reply all to include the entire interview panel
/: Jump to the search bar to find a specific resume

blocks.text: Your inbox can quickly become a mess of interview requests and candidate follow-ups. Use labels to categorize emails by role or hiring stage. Create a label for each active job requisition. You can also color-code them to see your priorities at a glance. If you need help setting this up, ask Lazur to guide you through the label creation menu. This keeps your communication organized and ensures you never miss a candidate update.

Recruiters spend too much time typing the same messages. Gmail templates, formerly known as canned responses, are your best friend here. Enable them in Settings > Advanced. Create templates for initial outreach, interview invitations, and rejection emails. When you need to send one, click the three dots in the compose window, select Templates, and choose your pre-written text. You can use Lazur to draft these templates once so you have a professional, consistent tone for every candidate.
How to handle email attachments for resumes

Handling resumes as attachments is a daily task. Gmail makes it easy to search for these files. Use the search operator has:attachment to find all emails that contain files. You can combine this with specific file types like has:attachment filename:pdf to find resumes specifically. This is much faster than scrolling through your inbox manually. If you are struggling with large files, remember that Gmail has a 25MB limit for attachments. For larger files, use Google Drive and share a link instead.
Using Lazur to speed up your recruitment workflow

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you manage your work without clicking through menus. Hold the Option + Command keys to ask a question about your screen. You can ask where a specific setting is, and Lazur will circle it for you. Hold the fn key to dictate emails directly into the Gmail compose window. This is perfect for those long candidate rejection letters or detailed feedback notes that take too long to type.

Interview scheduling is a major bottleneck. Use the Schedule Send feature in Gmail to set up interview reminders or follow-ups at the right time. Click the arrow next to the Send button to choose a time. This allows you to batch your scheduling tasks in the morning and have the emails go out throughout the day. It also helps you respect time zones when you are recruiting candidates across different regions.
Common mistakes to avoid in Gmail

Many recruiters forget to use BCC when emailing multiple candidates. This is a privacy disaster. Always put your own email in the To field and the candidates in the BCC field to keep their contact information private. Another common mistake is ignoring the display density settings. If your inbox feels too crowded, go to Settings > Display density and choose Comfortable. This gives you more breathing room to see your subject lines and labels clearly.

Beyond Gmail, you likely use LinkedIn, an ATS, and Notion. Keeping these tabs organized is a challenge. Consider using a tool like SupaSidebar to create a persistent sidebar in your browser. This keeps your most-used links within reach without cluttering your main work area. If you find yourself switching between too many apps, use the Mac Mission Control feature to group your recruitment windows on a specific desktop space.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native Gmail application for macOS. You should use a browser like Chrome or Safari, or create a web app shortcut for a native-like experience.

faq.question: How do I turn on keyboard shortcuts in Gmail?
faq.answer: Go to Settings in the top right, select See all settings, stay in the General tab, and scroll down to Keyboard shortcuts. Select Keyboard shortcuts on, then click Save changes at the bottom.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me write emails to candidates?
faq.answer: Yes, you can hold the fn key to dictate your email content directly into the compose box. Lazur ensures your text is clean and formatted correctly.

faq.question: How many recipients can I email at once?
faq.answer: For personal Gmail accounts, you are limited to 500 recipients per day. For Google Workspace accounts, the limit is typically 2,000 recipients per day.

faq.question: What should I do if my Gmail is slow or not connecting?
faq.answer: Check your internet connection first. Clear your browser cache or try opening Gmail in an Incognito window to rule out extension conflicts. If you see an error code, search the Gmail Help Center for that specific code.
